quest.title: Cooking, the Beauty of Sharing
quest.description: According to Arachatora, his brother Araphala is doing "cooking training" close by Devantaka Mountain. Look for a pillar of smoke near Devantaka Mountain!
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there!
*snore* *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Hello—!
Mmm... Tasty fruits... *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, he's in deep slumber. Oh, right. Arapacati mentioned that <color=#00E1FFFF>the power of Dendro</color> should do the trick.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon will leave it to you, {NICKNAME}.
Oh? It's you. Long time no see.
Whoa, where am I? Is this a cave? Ugh... I'm feeling dizzy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who are you? Why are you sleeping here?
Who am I... Ugh, so dizzy. Let me think... My name is...

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: My name is Araphala! Hehe, I remember now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're Araphala! We were wondering where you'd gone... and here you were, sleeping in this cave the whole time!

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Araphala... You know my name...

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Eh? Nara!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's wide awake now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Indeed he is.

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: *sob* I'm not ready yet. Don't make porridge out of me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why would anyone want to make porridge out of you!?

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: M—My sister said that if I'm always half asleep like this, a bad Nara will take me and make porridge out of me...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Waaah!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! {NICKNAME}, don't make jokes like that! Araphala, no one will cook you!

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: ...Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Not kidding?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No kidding! Anyway, Paimon's name is Paimon, and this tall Nara is {NICKNAME}. Arapacati sent us...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Arapacati? Is she doing well? How long have I been here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "How long," you say? Well, if Paimon recalls correctly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Many, many moons ago, the seedlings sprouted from the earth, and became trees... How many Arapacatis tall were they again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa! As expected of {NICKNAME}! What an amazing memory!

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Oh, it's been so long. Oh no.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's bring you up to speed. Festival Utsava is coming up...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You bring Araphala up to speed on the events so far...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Ah, it's time for Festival Utsava, is it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, so Arapacati wants you back in Vanarana.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Ugh... But I haven't completed my cooking training yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Weren't you sleeping? Paimon thought...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: "Sleeping"? Oh, I was just thinking about the past. It wasn't that serious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Is sleeping something serious for Aranara?

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Hmm... How should I put this... We hibernate when we are in grave danger, and we compress our memories and dreams into a seed.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: If the crisis is averted and the time is right, the seed will return to the forest and grow into Aranara again.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: But I know that all Nara must sleep. I had a Nara friend once, a Golden Nara just like you.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: #I once came here with {F#him}{M#her} to gather the Unrivaled Fresh Fruits.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: #So, I've been picking them here since then. If {F#he}{M#she} returns, or if I make new Nara friends, we can eat them together.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: I've picked so many of them this time... Eh? Where did they go?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, it's you who dropped those Sunsettias we saw all along the way.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Did I drop that many? But it's okay, hehe... I've kept the freshest and tastiest with me.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: But still... How did I drop so many...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: I remember leaving with my brothers for cooking training. But they didn't know that fresh fruits are the best ingredients...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: But while I was picking fruits... Yes, while I was picking fruits, a really huge monster appeared.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: That huge monster was five Araphalas tall and had a long tail. Even the ground quaked beneath its stomps. Besides that, I think I sensed Marana's aura inside it.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: And it was so tough! Even if Arama and Arabalika were there, it would take them some effort to tear it apart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait!? They are that strong!?

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Yes, but I'm not. So, I had to hide here. I was thinking about the past as I waited for it to leave, and the next thing I knew, you two were standing in front of me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, we did see a Ruin Drake on the way here. Is that the huge monster you mentioned?

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Is that how Nara call it? Perhaps. Very likely.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: #Whoa! I didn't expect Nara {NICKNAME} who looks smaller than the monster to be so strong!

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Alright, then let's go. Good Nara, let's eat fruits together.

choices.text: Ah, that huge monster! So scary!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Was it that scary though?

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Yes, looks like Nara understands that it's very scary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't worry. {NICKNAME} had defeated that huge monster before we met you!

choices.text: Paimon, can you turn into a seed?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, do you have any problem with Paimon!?

choices.text: Your memory is amazing as well, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee—hee...

choices.text: No one will make you into porridge.

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: *snore* *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Araphala!

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, it's Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, we are here to tell you that {NICKNAME} has taken down the huge monster outside!

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: #Whoa! I didn't expect Nara {NICKNAME} who looks smaller than the monster to be so strong!

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Alright, then let's go. Good Nara, let's eat fruits together.

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Okay, let's start cooking with the Unrivaled Fresh Fruits.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the difference between this "Unrivaled Fresh Fruit" and ordinary fruits?

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: I understand. To Nara, all fruits may be the same, but they are different.

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Only strong trees can bear Unrivaled Fresh Fruits. Strong trees sing first when the wind blows.

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: The bearings of the strong trees, these Unrivaled Fresh Fruits, are a blessing to us. That Nara friend said these fruits are so tasty they sing in your stomach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't wait to see what kind of delicacy will be made from them!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Araphala starts cooking right away...\nHe divides the fruits equally...\nThen, he gives a few portions to you and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You try the fresh fruits together.\nIt sort of lives up to your expectations. They do taste like fresh fruits.

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: So good. Thank you, strong trees.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! You call that cooking?

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: The Unrivaled Fresh Fruit itself is the best Supreme Delicacy. It doesn't need any extra processing to present its best taste...

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Just taste it and you will understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It is tasty, but it's just... it's just like eating fruits...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It is a fruit after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon guesses so...

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Don't you Nara have a dish where you cut fruits and serve them on a wooden board too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Do we? Wait! Are you talking about a fruit platter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is a fruit platter considered a dish?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It still seems a bit strange to Paimon...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Oh, don't be a stickler for things like that. Finding better ingredients is a form of cooking too.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: While searching for ingredients, I can travel the forest and get closer to it. That's the true meaning of my cooking training.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it?

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: It sure is.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: I've picked Unrivaled Fresh Fruits and made my Supreme Delicacy. My cooking training is complete.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: I can return proudly to Vanarana.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: #Oh, I would've missed Festival Utsava if Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon didn't take care of that huge monster that blocked me here in this cave.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, hurry back to Vanarana!

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Indeed, indeed... Sister will scold me if I miss Festival Utsava... Just the thought of it is scary enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? It's kinda strange to call something that hasn't been, y'know, processed... a dish.

talks.objective: Use Dendro to wake the Aranara up

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: I don't want to go outside while such a scary and huge monster is roaming the area. I'm sorry, my "sister."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon sees. But Festival Utsava is coming, you should return home.

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: Festival Utsava is meant to be carefree, but I'll care for my life if I leave this place. *snore* I can't do that for Festival Utsava...

response.speaker: Araphala
response.text: *snore* *snore* Nara Varuna...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... This guy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do we do, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Let's deal with the big scary monster.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon doesn't think anything can be scarier than Stormterror. In fact, Paimon wonders how Aranara would describe Stormterror?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "A million Araphalas tall!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "To walk from its tail to the head, the moon will rise and fall!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, let's help him deal with that monster outside.

dialogues.text: *snore* When will you be back? *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's wake him up once we take care of the monster...)

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: Festival Utsava is coming, I must... *snore* I must hurry up...

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: *snore* *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Leaf With Careful Penmanship
dialogues.text: (A huge leaf. Someone has written on it with neat handwriting...)

dialogues.speaker: Leaf With Careful Penmanship
dialogues.text: "...Leaves turned yellow. I picked a fresh and tasty Sunsettia."

dialogues.speaker: Leaf With Careful Penmanship
dialogues.text: "...Branches turned green. I didn't find any fruits..."

dialogues.speaker: Leaf With Careful Penmanship
dialogues.text: "Leaves are growing again, and 40 moons have passed. I picked Sunsettias outside the campsite and brought them back to Vanarana, but sister said they were still very unripe..."
